themes.theme: Testing Methodology and Routes to Compliance
themes.reason: This is the central implementation mechanism: it lays out the specific routes to compliance, the revised match test, and how choices were changed in response to stakeholder feedback, directly explaining how the intervention will be delivered and why this method was chosen over alternatives.

Defines which products are covered by the new regime and why certain exclusions are proposed, bearing on how the intervention will be rolled out and what alternatives (removing certain products) were considered; without this the implementation boundaries would be unclear.

Describes a specific administrative requirement for implementation but is a supporting/ancillary mechanism rather than a core pillar of the rollout method; it adds detail without being a necessary support for the overall case.

Explains the chosen timeline for rollout, including why the transition period was extended and the cost trade-offs considered, directly addressing how the intervention will be phased in and the reasoning/evidence behind that choice.

themes.theme: Cost Impacts and Evidence Base for Policy Development
themes.reason: These are general statements about testing assumptions and gathering more evidence through consultation, rather than substantive argument for the implementation method itself; removing them would not undermine the core rollout case.

Describes supportive measures (guidance, trade association engagement) that facilitate implementation but are secondary to the core testing/compliance and timeline decisions; the case for implementation could stand without this detail.
